The anatomy of a Cambrian accretion zone in the Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt: implications for Gondwanaland assembly

Abstract:

The Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt (EGMB) is a Proterozoic high-grade metamorphic belt along the eastern margin of the Indian Shield that preserves evidence of prolonged crustal evolution and multiple tectonometamorphic events. However, the structural relationship between the Western Charnockite Zone (WCZ)and the Eastern Ghats Province (EGP) and the regional continuity of the Sileru Shear Zone (SSZ) remain inadequately constrained. This study integrates field mapping, structural analysis, and petrographic investigations of charnockites and mafic granulites from the WCZ-EGP transition to elucidate the deformation history and metamorphic evolution of the region. The WCZ is dominated by garnet-free charnockites, mafic granulites, enderbites, quartzites, and calc-silicate rocks, whereas the EGP is characterized by blastoporphyritic garnet-bearing granitoids, khondalites, quartzofeldspathic gneisses, and mafic granulites. Field observations reveal an early D₁ gneissic fabric that was subsequently overprinted by a D₂ sinistral transpressional deformation associated with the SSZ, producing a penetrative NE-SW-trending foliation, mylonitization, grain-size reduction, folded and boudinaged leucosomes, and down-dip stretching lineations. Petrographic evidence, including garnet-quartz coronas around orthopyroxene, orthopyroxene-plagioclase symplectites replacing hornblende, two-stage garnet growth, flaser textures, chessboard extinction in quartz, and localized biotite replacement of orthopyroxene, records granulite-facies metamorphism accompanied by high-temperature ductile deformation and subsequent metamorphic re-equilibration. The progressive decrease in strain intensity away from the WCZ-EGP boundary demonstrates strong localization of deformation within the shear zone. The integrated structural and petrographic dataset delineates the continuation of the SSZ across the study area, extending its recognized trace and highlighting its significance as a major crustal-scale transpressional structure that controlled deformation, metamorphic reworking, and the tectonic architecture of the EGMB.
